items.summary: Update the global CSS custom properties in `frontend/src/index.css` to use a softer, eye-friendly color palette: replace the current parchment/cream background with a slightly warmer but lower-saturation tone (e.g., #f7f3ec or similar), reduce the harshness of dark teal accents by softening them to a muted medium teal, and ensure all foreground/body text colors use dark values with a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against their backgrounds (WCAG AA minimum). The gold accent should be darkened enough to remain legible as text.

Audit and fix text color declarations in `QuizScreen.tsx`, `ReviewScreen.tsx`, `ResultsScreen.tsx`, `AdminPanelScreen.tsx`, `TopicBrowserScreen.tsx`, `HistoryScreen.tsx`, `HomeScreen.tsx`, `SubscriptionPlansScreen.tsx`, and `AppHeader.tsx` to ensure every text element (question text, option labels, headings, stat numbers, form labels, menu links) uses a clearly visible, high-contrast color against its background. Replace any instance where text color matches or is too close to the background color — particularly on highlighted/selected states, card surfaces, and header areas.

Update `frontend/tailwind.config.js` color token definitions (and any OKLCH values used for primary, foreground, muted, accent, and card tokens) to align with the new eye-friendly palette: use lower-saturation, medium-brightness values for backgrounds and softer but sufficiently dark values for text tokens. Ensure the Tailwind theme tokens are consistent with the CSS custom properties updated in REQ-52 so utility classes like `text-foreground`, `bg-card`, `text-primary`, and `text-muted-foreground` all produce accessible, eye-friendly results.
